reports.dimension_interpretation: Partition-level structural diagnostics provide triage evidence about the candidate-generation consensus geometry. For all three candidate sets, the dominant spectral gap is at the single-cluster resolution (screen_candidate_k=1), so the internal screen does not show a dominant multi-cluster subdivision signal. Within-set affinities are moderate to relatively high (0.51–0.68), while between-set affinities are lower (0.22–0.25), indicating that the current partition separates the candidate sets in the consensus geometry. The nearest competing boundary is K3_C0001–K3_C0002 (mean between affinity 0.249), followed by K3_C0002–K3_C0003 (0.234) and K3_C0001–K3_C0003 (0.217). These observations describe the current partition structure and identify pair-review entry points; they do not establish biological meaning, clinical validity, or prescribe retention, split, or merge actions.

evidence_reports.dimension_interpretation: At partition scope, global GRV measures overall shared structure between modality patient geometries. Three modality pairs show significant concordance after permutation testing: WSI–RNA (GRV 0.198, p=0.001), CT–WSI (GRV 0.167, p=0.001), and RNA–WXS (GRV 0.145, p=0.001). Three pairs are nonsignificant: CT–WXS (GRV 0.103, p=0.218), CT–RNA (GRV 0.092, p=0.071), and WSI–WXS (GRV 0.092, p=0.096). The significant pairs involve WSI and RNA as recurring partners, while CT and WXS participate mainly in nonsignificant pairs. Magnitudes are modest across all pairs (GRV 0.09–0.20), and bootstrap intervals are wide, so the concordance is real but limited. This is partition-level patient-geometry concordance only; it does not establish mechanistic agreement, independent validation, or candidate-specific membership, and it does not by itself establish biological meaning or clinical validity.
